subject: Pilot capacity: temporary reserved slice & autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Rory Quinn <rory.quinn@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health - InfraOps <infra@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood pilot — brief ask on reserved capacity for POC

Marcus — thanks again for the demo last week. Nimbus is ready to kick off a 6-week pilot that will exercise our EHR-derived search use case (bursty daytime traffic, large context windows). Before legal finishes the SOW we need to lock a short-term capacity plan to guarantee latency while we validate cost and throughput.

Ask: can Redwood carve out a temporary reserved slice (preferably 8 GPU equivalents) for 2027-01-03 to 2027-02-14 with an autoscale exception that allows burst to 12 GPUs for 2x daily peak windows? We also need read-only access to per-token latency traces for our eval team.

I've attached a high-level pilot statement of work and a baseline metrics file. Happy to jump on a call — Rory

Attachments: nimbus-pilot-ma.pdf, pilot-metrics-baseline.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rory Quinn <rory.quinn@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — brief ask on reserved capacity for POC

Rory — thanks, looping in Kim (enterprise sales) and Laura (solutions/ops) to scope feasibility. High level: we can usually grant short-term reserved slices, but the autoscale exception is a support/ops decision and needs product signoff on routing/fallback behavior.

Next steps from our side:
- Laura, can you run a quick capacity check against Jan 3–Feb 14 and confirm whether 8 dedicated GPUs + 12 burst is constraining on current pools?
- Karthik and Dev (cc'd via follow-up) — product question: are there any gating concerns for exposing per-token latency traces to an external eval team (read-only) under a pilot agreement?

Rory — we'll aim to get an internal response within two business days and propose a few carveout options.

Thanks,
Marcus
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — brief ask on reserved capacity for POC

Quick infrastructure check: I've run the 8+4 burst scenario against our projected pool utilization for the us-west region. Findings:
- January baseline (existing commitments) leaves ~14 GPU equivalents of slack across pilot-capable pools between Jan 2–10, but slack drops to ~6 by Jan 20 if other reserved pilots start.
- Allowing burst to 12 for two short windows/day is feasible if we create a carved lane with preemptible reservations and a hard policy that routes overflow to our non-dedicated cold pool with a degraded model variant fallback.
- Risk: if multiple enterprise pilots request burst simultaneously we will hit contention; mitigation is a soft queue + auction fallback.

I recommend we propose a 6-week reserved carveout that guarantees 8 GPUs and a documented burst policy (max 12; burst only in two 45-min windows/day). I'll attach a capacity matrix with the week-by-week risk flags.

Attachments: q4-capacity-matrix.xlsx

Laura
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — brief ask on reserved capacity for POC

Thanks Laura — product notes:
- Per-token latency traces: we can provide a redacted, read-only view via a temporary dashboard that exposes token-level percentiles and example traces, but we must strip user PHI from any exported traces. Legal will need to approve the exact fields; recommend we commit to "aggregate + sampled traces" rather than full raw logs.
- Autoscale exception: we should not create an open exception path; instead propose a guarded-exception workflow: (1) pre-authorized burst windows (dates/times) submitted at provisioning, (2) automated gate that enforces model-variant fallback if total cluster saturation > 85%, (3) alerting to ops and account owner.

If everyone is aligned, I'll draft the exception policy language and the changes needed in routing config.

Karthik
Director, Product — Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rory Quinn <rory.quinn@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T17:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — brief ask on reserved capacity for POC

Rory — thanks for patience. Internal alignment summary and ask for confirmation:
- We can offer a 6-week reserved carveout (2027-01-03 to 2027-02-14) guaranteeing 8 GPU equivalents in the us-west pool.
- We will allow burst to 12 GPUs limited to two pre-scheduled 45-minute windows per business day. Bursts are subject to an automated gate: if cluster saturation is above 85% at the scheduled start, the system will fall back to the next-compatible model variant (slightly higher latency, lower cost) and notify both Nimbus and Redwood ops.
- We will provide a redacted, read-only dashboard with sampled per-token latency percentiles and example traces; no raw PHI will be exported.
- Attachments: updated capacity matrix and the proposed exception policy language.

Please confirm these constraints so we can encode them into the SOW and provision the carveout by Dec 15. If you need the burst windows to align to a different timezone, indicate preferred start/end slots and we will try to align.

Kim, Laura, Karthik, Dev — next action: Karthik please draft the exception policy doc; Laura please prepare the provisioning ticket with pre-provisioned pool IDs; Kim please confirm commercial terms & work with finance to draft a short addendum. Target: provision by 2026-12-15.

Thanks,
Marcus
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
